curriculum.lesson_evidence: Ancient societies can be studied through beliefs, daily life and social structure, always limited by surviving evidence. Describe patterns from sources without claiming every person lived the same way. Avoid presenting religious ideas as facts about the supernatural; present them as beliefs recorded in sources.
curriculum.scope_limit: Proposed Stage 4 NESA HSIE alignment using catalogue outcome code HT4-2; content-point mapping remains pending. Local First Nations protocols and Community verification remain pending human review. Do not invent Country names, Dreaming stories, sacred knowledge or unverified cultural claims.

lesson.child_mission: Ancient societies can be studied through beliefs, daily life and social structure, always limited by surviving evidence. Describe patterns from sources without claiming every person lived the same way. Avoid presenting religious ideas as facts about the supernatural; present them as beliefs recorded in sources.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same HSIE idea to a new place or source, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Using class sources, name one belief practice, one daily-life activity and one social role, each with a source note.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: Three evidenced points; wording treats beliefs as beliefs; no invented sacred Australian content.

WATCH FOR
Assuming ancient art shows photography-like reality. Art can be symbolic or idealised.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Build a three-column society chart (beliefs / daily life / structure) with six sourced entries and two 'unknown from these sources' notes.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: In a river valley society, irrigation shaped farming calendars; temple records may show elite religion more than private belief. Daily life for labourers may appear mainly in art or archaeology.

TRY FIRST
Using class sources, name one belief practice, one daily-life activity and one social role, each with a source note.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: Three evidenced points; wording treats beliefs as beliefs; no invented sacred Australian content.
teach_steps.explain:
Ancient societies can be studied through beliefs, daily life and social structure, always limited by surviving evidence. Describe patterns from sources without claiming every person lived the same way. Avoid presenting religious ideas as facts about the supernatural; present them as beliefs recorded in sources.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the sources, map features or community examples that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a detail is uncertain, identify what source you would need next. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Assuming ancient art shows photography-like reality. Art can be symbolic or idealised. Correct the claim or use of sources, not just the neatness of the poster.
